subject: Clarifications: copies, backups, and certificate of deletion for EU accounts
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@northshorehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@northshorehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about copies, backups, and deletion certification

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for sending over the DPA redline. We had a quick pass and our legal ops team flagged a couple of items that need clarifying before we can sign:

1) Copies and backups: the redline says Redwood will delete "customer data" within 45 days of termination, but LegalOps needs to know how you treat copies (snapshots, replication, backups) stored for durability. Do those get purged on the same schedule, or do you maintain longer retention for backups?

2) Proof of deletion: we often need a certificate of deletion for our records — can Redwood provide a signed confirmation when data is erased, and what is the scope of that confirmation (primary data only, or backups too)?

3) Onshore access: since we are a European healthcare provider, we need assurance that any onshore access to EU-hosted data (for debugging or support) is logged and subject to the same deletion commitments.

Attached are our annotated redlines (NSH_DPA_redlines_v2.docx). Can you confirm the answers and propose any alternative wording? We are aiming to finalize this week if possible.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Bennett
Head of Legal Operations
NorthShore Health

Attachments: NSH_DPA_redlines_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: LegalOps <legal@northshorehealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about copies, backups, and deletion certification

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick review and the annotated file. Looping in our legal (Irene) and infra (Mina, Marcus) to provide concrete answers. High level answers below while they confirm specifics:

- Backups/copies: Our permanent backups (cold snapshots kept for disaster recovery) are retained up to 90 days by default; ephemeral snapshots and caches are removed per the 45-day erasure window after termination except where a legal hold applies.

- Certificate of deletion: We can provide a signed deletion attestation for the customer tenant and primary production data within 45 days of termination. For backups, we can provide an attestation confirming we will purge backups in accordance with the backup retention window (we will include the retention window in the attestation).

- Onshore support access: All support/debug access to EU-hosted data is logged and goes through an approval flow; access is limited to approved engineers and is covered by the same contractual confidentiality controls. We will include a logging and audit reference in the DPA appendix.

Irene / Mina / Marcus — could you confirm the exact backup retention details and propose a short clause we can add to the DPA to make this explicit? Sarah — would a two-line attestation (one line for primary data deletion within 45 days, one line describing backup purge timing) be acceptable, or do you need a more granular timeline per backup tier?

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

--

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@northshorehealth.com>, LegalOps <legal@northshorehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about copies, backups, and deletion certification

Jordan / Irene / Marcus — infra notes below to use in the DPA language. I added a short plain-English explanation that we can surface in the appendix or playbook: 

1) Backup tiers and retention windows (EU-hosted):
- Live replicas / synchronous replication: 0 - these are not separate durable copies; they are part of production cluster 
- Short-term snapshots: retained for up to 7 days for rollback/ops (encrypted at rest)
- Disaster-recovery cold backups: retained for up to 90 days (encrypted at rest, geo-redundant within EU)
- Long-term compliance archives: not created by default; only if customer opts in — those are covered by a separate retention schedule and explicit acceptance.

2) Erasure behavior on termination:
- Primary data and short-term snapshots: deleted within 45 days of termination (this aligns with our standard erasure pipeline).
- Cold backups: scheduled for purge at the end of the next backup cycle but no later than 90 days from termination. We can set the DPA to commit to "purge within 90 days for DR backups".

3) Certificate of deletion: We can generate a signed deletion attestation that references both the primary deletion (45 days) and the cold backup purge (90 days). The attestation will include: tenant ID, deletion job run IDs, S3 snapshot IDs (redacted as needed), and timestamp range.

4) Onshore access: Any access originating from non-EU regions to EU-hosted data requires an access ticket and is audited; logs are retained for 12 months and we can include an audit-sampling clause for customer review.

I propose the following short contract snippet for the DPA appendix (one sentence each):
- "Redwood will permanently delete Customer Data from production systems and short-term snapshots within forty-five (45) days following termination or expiration of services, subject to lawful hold."
- "Disaster-recovery backups will be purged within ninety (90) days following termination or expiration of services unless Customer has requested a separate archival arrangement in writing."
- "Upon Customer request after completion of the purge windows, Redwood will provide a signed attestation describing the scope and timing of the deletions."

If that language is acceptable, Irene can feed it back into the DPA redline and we can return to Sarah with a draft attestation template.

— Mina
Sr. Prod Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: erase-playbook-summary.pdf (PDF summary of purge workflow)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@northshorehealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about copies, backups, and deletion certification

Sarah — thanks for raising these. I reviewed Mina's proposed wording and made two legal-focused tweaks to reduce ambiguity and limit operational burden:

1) Replace "permanently delete" with "render unrecoverable by Redwood" for production systems — this captures typical secure-delete semantics for distributed systems where low-level forensic residuals may exist in immutable media.

2) For the attestation, Redwood will provide a certificate that indicates the categories and timing of deletion (production data: within 45 days; DR backups: within 90 days) rather than enumerating internal snapshot IDs. If NorthShore needs forensic-level proof we can handle that under a separate eDiscovery/forensics request with mutually agreed scope and cost.

Suggested DPA redline excerpts (one-line insertions):
- "Redwood will render Customer Data stored in production systems and short-term snapshots unrecoverable within forty-five (45) days after termination or expiration of services, except to the extent preservation is required by law."
- "Redwood will purge disaster‑recovery backups within ninety (90) days following termination or expiration of services unless Customer has requested and paid for a separate archival arrangement."
- "Upon request, Redwood will issue a deletion attestation describing the scope and timing of the purges; such attestation will not include internal snapshot identifiers but will reference the tenant and the date ranges covered."

If that approach is acceptable to NorthShore, we'll update the DPA and attach a blank attestation template for signature. Jordan — want me to push the redline back to Sarah with the attestation template?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions about copies, backups, and deletion certification

Sarah / LegalOps — thanks for the patience. We made the updates and attached the attestation template. Summary and concrete commitments below so we can close the loop: 

1) Production data and short-term snapshots: Redwood will render customer data unrecoverable within 45 days of termination (subject to lawful hold).
2) Disaster-recovery cold backups: Redwood will purge these within 90 days of termination unless Customer requests an archival arrangement in writing.
3) Attestation: Redwood will provide a signed deletion attestation after the relevant purge windows that references the tenant, date ranges, and attestation IDs. The attestation does not include internal snapshot S3 object names; if NorthShore requires that level of detail we can scope a separate forensic confirmation.
4) Onshore access & logging: Any support access to EU-hosted data is ticketed and logged; logs are retained 12 months and available for audit sampling.

Next steps: please confirm via reply if the three bullets above meet NorthShore's needs. If yes, we will send an updated DPA PDF with the new appendix language and the attestation template attached. For tracking, I have logged this in HubSpot (HS-Contact-12345).

Appended: "Deletion Attestation Template" (attached as PDF) and the updated DPA redline (NSH_DPA_redlines_v3.docx).

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
